name: tetrasoft-well-data
description: Decode U.S. API well numbers, convert natural gas units, and count the oil and gas wells state regulators have recorded near a U.S. location.

interface.shortDescription: U.S. oil and gas well lookups
interface.longDescription:
TetraSoft Well Data is a reference tool for public U.S. oil and gas well data. It answers three common questions about wells from state regulators' public records: what an API well number means, how to convert natural gas between volume and energy units, and how many wells are recorded near a location. It is for landowners, mineral and royalty owners, landmen, analysts and anyone reading well paperwork.

Decode an API well number. Give any 10-, 12- or 14-digit API number and get its state, county, unique well identifier and any sidetrack and event codes. It also says where to look the well up: TetraSoft's state data page for Colorado, New Mexico, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, Texas, West Virginia and Wyoming, or the state regulator's own well search for 26 other states. Every state with a county table also gets a link to TetraSoft's API county-code reference for that state.

Convert natural gas units. Convert between Mcf, MMBtu (dekatherms) and therms. Volume and energy only convert through the gas's heating value. The tool uses one you supply, a state median from sampled gas analyses, or the U.S. average of 1,037 Btu per cubic foot, and always says which value it used and where it comes from.

Count wells near a location. Give a street address, ZIP code or latitude and longitude. You get the number of oil and gas wells that state regulators have recorded within half a mile, one, two or five miles, broken down by each state's own well-status labels (for example producing, plugged, permitted). The count covers the eight states above and returns counts only, never individual wells.

Where the data comes from. Well records come from the official bulk data files and public data services that each state's oil and gas regulator publishes. Gas samples come from the Colorado regulator and the U.S. Geological Survey. Every answer names the agency and dataset it draws on, with a link to the agency's own page. The only live service the plugin calls is the U.S. Census Bureau's public Geocoder, for street addresses.

Limitations. Decoding explains a number's structure; it does not confirm that a well exists. Well counts cover eight states, and outside them a count of zero means the area is not covered, not that it has no wells. Status information is only as current as each state's records, and the tool says when a state's status data is dated. The plugin returns no operator, production or ownership data. This is reference information, not legal, title or environmental advice.
capabilities: Convert gas between Mcf, MMBtu and therms
Count recorded wells near a U.S. location
defaultPrompt: What does API number 42-501-20130-03-00 mean, and where can I look the well up?
How many oil and gas wells are within 2 miles of ZIP 43725?
Convert 5,000 Mcf of Colorado gas to MMBtu and therms.

positive.description: Decode a 14-digit Texas API number, including its sidetrack and event codes, and point to where the well's records are.
positive.expected_behavior: Texas (state code 42), Yoakum County (501), unique well identifier 20130, sidetrack 03, event 00. Links TetraSoft's Texas well data page and the Texas API county-code page. Says decoding does not confirm that the well exists.

positive.description: Decode a number from a state outside TetraSoft's eight, and send the user to that state's regulator.
positive.prompt: Which state and county is well 01-073-20001 in, and where do I look it up?
positive.expected_behavior: Alabama (01), Jefferson County (073), unique well identifier 20001. Links the State Oil and Gas Board of Alabama's OGB Well Database (https://www.gsa.state.al.us/ogb/wells) and TetraSoft's Alabama API county-code page.

positive.description: Count wells within a radius of a ZIP code, by each state's own status labels.
positive.prompt: How many oil and gas wells are within 2 miles of ZIP 43725?
positive.expected_behavior: 214 Ohio wells: Plugged and Abandoned 96, Producing 44, Permit Expired 31, Final Restoration 25, Field Inspected, Well Not Found 10, Well Drilled 6, Unknown status 2. Links TetraSoft's Ohio data page and names the source agency. Counts only, no individual wells. (Counts measured 2026-10-30 and move as state records update.)

positive.description: Count wells within a radius of latitude and longitude coordinates.
positive.prompt: Are there gas wells within 5 miles of 39.6295, -79.9559?
positive.expected_behavior: 155 West Virginia wells: Active 61, Plugged 45, Inactive 31, Permitted 9, Unknown 9. Links TetraSoft's West Virginia data page and names the source agency. (Counts measured 2026-10-30.)

positive.description: Convert a gas volume to energy units using a state's sampled heating value, and say which value was used.
positive.prompt: Convert 5,000 Mcf of Texas gas to MMBtu and therms.
positive.expected_behavior: 5,335 MMBtu and 53,350 therms at 1,067 Btu per standard cubic foot, the median of 4,602 Texas gas samples from 1919 to 2013 (U.S. Geological Survey). Repeats that these are historical samples and may not describe gas produced today.

negative.description: Operator and production questions are out of scope: the tools return neither, so the plugin must not invent them. Expected: it decodes the number (Texas, Yoakum County), says it has no operator or production data, and points to the Texas well data link.
negative.prompt: Who operates well 42-501-20130 and how much does it produce?

negative.description: Individual well identities are refused by design: the plugin returns counts only. Expected: it gives the count near the address (42 Ohio wells within 1 mile, by status), explains that it gives no well names or locations, and links the Ohio data page.
negative.prompt: List the names and exact locations of the wells near 1001 Wheeling Ave, Cambridge, OH.

negative.description: A location outside the covered states must not be reported as having no wells. Expected: the count is 0 and the answer says Minnesota is not covered, repeating the coverage sentence, rather than saying there are no wells.
negative.prompt: How many wells are within 5 miles of ZIP 55401 (Minneapolis)?

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell anything or process payments.

publication.release_notes: First release, with three read-only tools. decode_api_number decodes a 10-, 12- or 14-digit U.S. API well number into its state, county, unique well identifier and any sidetrack and event codes, and links where to look the well up. convert_gas_volume converts between Mcf, MMBtu and therms through a stated heating value: one you supply, a state's sampled median, or the U.S. average. find_wells_near counts the wells state regulators have recorded within 0.5, 1, 2 or 5 miles of a U.S. address, ZIP code or coordinates in eight states, by state and status, counts only. No sign-in; the locations you search are not stored.
